james.name: James Carter
james.bio: Licensed special investigator with unusual authority: he investigates, and he brings accusations to court. Newly certified. His father died when he was young — officially a disgrace. James does not believe the official part.

hayes.name: Michael Hayes
hayes.bio: Twenty-eight years in the field before the academy. Teaches one rule above all: evidence first, accusation second. He knew James's father. He has never said so out loud.
hayes.secret: In 2004, as a young detective, Hayes signed the evidence transfer that put Robert Carter's file into the archive — three weeks before the fire.

sarah.name: Sarah Miller
sarah.bio: The best forensic analyst in the county and the first ally James earns. Reads autopsies like confessions. Protective of her brother Marcus. Talks to the dead because the living lie.
sarah.secret: In 2019 she was coerced into re-signing a false autopsy addendum. The Registry keeps a copy. This is why they can hurt her.

marcus.name: Marcus Miller
marcus.bio: Sarah's older brother. A quiet, stubborn homicide detective who noticed that records cases spook people before anyone else said it out loud.

emma.name: Emma Reed
emma.bio: Assigned as James's courtroom counterpart. Sharp, procedural, secretly idealistic. Believes the record is the only weapon that cannot be stolen — which is why it terrifies her when it can.

wilson.name: Judge Marcus Wilson
wilson.bio: Strict, precise, allergic to sloppy evidence. Presides over most county inquests. In 2004 he was a junior court clerk on a case file numbered 404. He has never spoken about it.
wilson.secret: Wilson kept a personal copy of the 404 docket after the fire. It is hidden inside the courthouse.

helen.name: Helen Voss
helen.bio: Nineteen years cataloguing the county's memory. Found dead in the annex vault hallway on the night of October 4. She was careful. That is what killed her.

tomas.name: Tomas Verne
tomas.bio: Night guard with a smoking habit and a bad memory for times. Easily frightened, easily blamed. Tells the truth slowly, in pieces.

bishop.name: Alan Bishop
bishop.bio: Twenty-two years managing county records. Helen's supervisor. For years he sold sign-off alterations to people who needed the past rewritten. Helen found the dates. He panicked.

kessler.name: Victor Kessler
kessler.bio: The county's most expensive lawyer and the owner of Aegis Security. Requests files, attends funerals, wins cases. Legally. Always legally.
kessler.secret: Kessler executes the Registry's erasures. In 2004, as a junior fixer, he drafted the falsified evidence report that destroyed Robert Carter.

nina.name: Nina Park
nina.bio: Helen Voss's neighbor and the waitress who saw too much at the Veridian. Frightened of attention. The kind of witness that cases break against.

daniel.name: Daniel Fox
daniel.bio: James's rival in training. Fast, arrogant, allergic to procedure. Stole a medal out of panic. There are worse people in this city. He will meet several of them.

gus.name: Gus Bloom
gus.bio: Forty years keeping the academy standing. Polishes the display case every day at six. Knows every key and every shadow in the building.

priya.name: Priya Nair
priya.bio: First exam cycle, terrified of blame. Remembers corridors better than she wants to.

hale.name: Richard Hale
hale.bio: The DA. James's ultimate superior. Charming, patient, untouchable. Personally assigns James the records beat — and personally congratulates him when cases close quietly.
hale.secret: Hale founded the Registry. In 2004, as a rising prosecutor, he buried CASE 404 and framed Robert Carter to protect the men who funded his career.

okafor.name: Sam Okafor
okafor.bio: Saw nothing. Officially. Keeps a private maintenance log because he does not trust paper that other people can find.

bell.name: Marcus Bell
bell.bio: Northbridge's outside accountant. Kept a second ledger because he did not trust his own memory. Found floating two weeks after CASE 006 opened.

rhea.name: Rhea Voss
rhea.bio: Helen Voss's younger sister. Investigates fires for a living. Started that way. Will not stop until the 2004 archive fire has a name attached.
